/**
 * The translator's bench for the three-pass method (src/i18n/TRANSLATING.md).
 *
 *   npm run i18n:tx -- pending <fr|zh>
 *       every dictionary that still holds an empty entry, with the count
 *   npm run i18n:tx -- show <page-id> [fr|zh]
 *       the page's own units (shared ones left out), numbered in reading
 *       order with their tag; with a locale, only the units still empty in it
 *   npm run i18n:tx -- build <fr|zh> <page-id>
 *       merge the pass files into the dictionary, then check the whole file
 *       against the house rules (scripts/i18n-rules.mjs); exit 1 on a
 *       problem or an entry still empty
 *
 * page-id: the dictionary's name under src/i18n/dict/<locale>/pages/
 * (home, pricing, resources/insights/<slug>...), or `common` for the shared
 * dictionary (show and build then need the locale; its units are numbered in
 * the order of that locale's common.json).
 *
 * Reading order and tags come from the context files written by
 *   npm run i18n:local -- extract --context .i18n-work/ctx
 * Run that first, and again after any change to an English page.
 *
 * Pass files, in .i18n-work/passes/<locale>/<page-id>/ :
 *   pass1*.json  {"<index>": "<translation>"}  Step 1, every index to translate
 *                (a long page may be split: pass1-a.json, pass1-b.json...)
 *   pass2.json   only the indexes Step 2 changed
 *   pass3.json   only the indexes Step 3 changed
 *   changes.md   10 to 40 lines: the main before/after across the passes
 * Later passes win (pass1 < pass2 < pass3). build writes only the indexes
 * found in the pass files: every other translation in the dictionary stays
 * as it is, so a changed page never loses its edited sentences.
 *
 * .i18n-work/ is ignored by git. Same file in the other site's repository
 * (hubstudio / BearingBridgeCOM): keep the two in step.
 */
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { problems } from './i18n-rules.mjs';

const root = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');
const DICT = join(root, 'src', 'i18n', 'dict');
const WORK = join(root, '.i18n-work');
const CTX = join(WORK, 'ctx');
const LOCALES = ['fr', 'zh'];

const readJson = (f) => (existsSync(f) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(f, 'utf8')) : {});
const writeJson = (f, data) => {
  mkdirSync(dirname(f), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(f, JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) + '\n');
};
const walk = (d) =>
  existsSync(d)
    ? readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((e) => (e.isDirectory() ? walk(join(d, e.name)) : [join(d, e.name)]))
    : [];
const rel = (f) => relative(root, f).replace(/\\/g, '/');
const idOf = (base, file) => relative(base, file).replace(/\\/g, '/').replace(/\.json$/, '');
const dictFile = (locale, id) => (id === 'common' ? join(DICT, locale, 'common.json') : join(DICT, locale, 'pages', `${id}.json`));
const fail = (msg) => {
  console.error(`âœ -  ${msg}`);
  process.exit(2);
};
const needLocale = (l) => {
  if (!LOCALES.includes(l)) fail(`locale must be ${LOCALES.join(' or ')}`);
};

/** Tag and page of every key, from the context files. */
function keyInfo() {
  const info = new Map();
  for (const f of walk(CTX)) {
    const ctx = readJson(f);
    for (const u of ctx.units ?? []) if (!info.has(u.key)) info.set(u.key, { tag: u.tag, attr: u.attr, path: ctx.path });
  }
  return info;
}

/** The units a dictionary is built from, in order: [{key, tag, attr}]. */
function unitsOf(locale, id) {
  if (id === 'common') {
    const info = keyInfo();
    return Object.keys(readJson(dictFile(locale, 'common'))).map((key) => ({ key, ...(info.get(key) ?? { tag: '?' }) }));
  }
  const file = join(CTX, `${id}.json`);
  if (!existsSync(file)) fail(`no context for ${id}: run  npm run i18n:local -- extract --context .i18n-work/ctx`);
  return readJson(file).units.filter((u) => !u.common);
}

<!-- SECTION: What changes per market -->

## What should change in a visual from one market to the next?

Start from what stays. Sort every element before anything is rendered, and
keep the list with the brief.

| Element | Keep or change | How |
|---|---|---|
| Product | Keep | Never regenerated per market; it stays from the master |
| Light, framing, palette | Keep | Shared by every version |
| Headline and offer copy | Change | Overlay layer per language, from the approved copy deck |
| Legal line or required label | Change where a market requires it | Overlay from the legal team's approved wording |
| Casting | Change only if the market needs it | Edit an image with source pictures |
| Setting and props | Change only if the market needs it | Edit an image, product kept |
| Text inside the scene (a sign, a label) | Change per language | Rendered in, then proofed by a native reader |

Write the reason next to every "change." When nobody can give one, the
element stays as it is in the master.

## How do you add each market's text as a layer you can edit?

Open the master in the Image editor. It's free and runs in your browser;
you can open it from the image studio, History or the Assets Library.

- Click Add text, or double-click the picture where the line should go, then
  type the first market's copy.
- Pick the font and size, then bold, italic or underline and the alignment.
- Set the color. A dark outline or a soft shadow keeps light words readable
  on a light picture; a highlight behind the words works on a busy one.
- Place the brand logo from the Picture panel, in one of nine positions.

# Deep Translate: three-pass native rewrite

Drive a page from "translated and too familiar" to "a native editor wrote
this." The user gives you two inputs: the **target language** and the **page**
(a file path to a localized page, or an i18n strings file). If either is
missing, ask for it before starting.

This skill ships with `HUMANIZER.md` (in this skill folder), a catalogue of
AI-writing tells and how to strip them. Read it before you start if you have
not already. It backs Step 1 below. If the host project also defines its own
translation/house-style rules (e.g. in a `CLAUDE.md` or style guide), honor
those too; they take precedence where they conflict with this skill. The
locale page is editorial state, not draft state: improve it, do not blindly
regenerate from English.

## Core standard (applies to every step)

- The result must read as **written, not spoken**. No casual, chatty, overly
  familiar register. Target a serious daily/business paper in that market:
  FR Le Monde / Les Echos, ES El País, ZH 财经 / 36氪, DE FAZ / Handelsblatt.
- **100% native, zero mistakes.** Grammar, idiom, collocation, rhythm,
  punctuation, and diacritics all at journalist/editor level.
- **Locale conventions are mandatory:** full diacritics (never ship unaccented
  copy), locale punctuation (ZH full-width `。，、：；！？""''（）`; FR guillemets
  `« »` with non-breaking spaces and NBSP before `: ; ! ?`; ES `¿ ¡`; DE `„…"`),
  and locale formatting for dates, currency, units, numbers.
- **Preserve structure:** headings, anchors, IDs, frontmatter keys, component
  props, ARIA labels, and any HTML/JSX stay intact. You are rewriting
  human-facing copy only, never code or identifiers.
- **SEO fields are in scope and must be rewritten too** (see below). They are
  prose, so they get the same native, journalist-grade treatment as body copy
  across all three passes, not left as-is.
- Honor any house rules the host project defines (banned words or characters,
  brand-name handling, subject/framing constraints). Apply them alongside the
  standards above.

## SEO fields are part of the rewrite

Every visitor- or search-facing string is prose and gets rewritten natively
across all three passes, exactly like body copy. Do not skip, freeze, or
merely "flag" these. Treat them as sections in their own right and show
before/after for each one you change:

- `<title>` / page title and the H1.
- meta description.
- OpenGraph copy: `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image:alt`.
- Twitter/X card copy: `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`.
- JSON-LD / schema.org human-readable fields: `name`, `headline`,
  `description`, `alternativeHeadline`, `caption`, FAQ `question`/`answer` text.
- Image `alt` text and figure captions.
- Any SEO-oriented microcopy: breadcrumb labels, structured-data text.

Hold these to the same bar as the rest: native journalistic register, full
diacritics, locale punctuation, no AI tells. A meta description or og:title
that still reads translated is a failed pass. Keep them accurate to the page
and within sensible length (title ~60 chars, meta description ~150–160), but
write them as a native SEO editor would, not as a literal rendering of the
English tag.

**Slugs are the one exception.** A slug is a URL, not prose. Do not rewrite it
silently as part of these passes: changing a live slug breaks inbound links and
routing. If a slug is non-native or English under a non-English locale, flag
the mismatch and propose a native, URL-safe, diacritic-stripped slug plus a
redirect from the old one, and only change it once the user agrees. Everything
else above is rewritten without asking.

## How to show changes "bit by bit"

Work through the page **section by section in document order**. For each
section you change, post a short before/after to the user like this:

```
[Section: hero subhead]
- before: <old target-language text>
+ after:  <new target-language text>
why: <one short line on what was unnatural and what register you moved to>
```

Then apply the Edit. Move to the next section. Do not dump the whole page at
once; reveal it gradually as you go. Sections that already read perfectly
native: say "kept as-is" and move on  -  but this shortcut applies **only to
Steps 2 and 3**. Step 1 rewrites every section from scratch with no
exceptions (see Step 1 below).

## The three steps

The whole point is escalation. Each step assumes the previous one was **still
not native enough** and pushes further. Do not stop early because a step "looks
fine"  -  the next step exists precisely to find what still reads translated.

### Step 1  -  Full native rewrite from scratch (NOT read-and-correct)

This step is a **complete rewrite**, not a proofreading pass. Do not read the
existing copy and patch the awkward bits. Rewrite **every section** from the
ground up, as if a native journalist were writing this page originally with a
blank sheet, then reconcile it with the original only to keep the facts,
structure, and meaning intact.

The mindset is: throw out the existing phrasing entirely and re-author the
content natively. Use the source page only for **what** to say (facts, claims,
numbers, structure), never for **how** to say it. Every sentence must be
re-composed from scratch in native register, not lifted, lightly edited, or
reordered from the existing text. This covers the **SEO fields** above
(title, meta description, OG/Twitter copy, schema text, alt text) just as much
as the body: re-author each one from scratch in native register. Apply the
AI-tell patterns in `HUMANIZER.md` as you write.

- Do **not** keep a sentence just because it is "already correct" or "good
  enough." Rewrite it anyway. Correct-but-translated still gets rebuilt.
- Do **not** do sentence-by-sentence touch-ups. Re-author each section as a
  whole so the native rhythm and flow come from the new draft, not the old one.
- Fix register first (spoken/familiar → written/journalistic), then idiom,
  collocation, rhythm, punctuation, diacritics  -  but always inside a freshly
  written sentence, never as edits to the original one.

If a "kept as-is" instinct shows up in Step 1, override it: in this step,
nothing is kept as-is. (Reserve "kept as-is" for Steps 2 and 3, which polish
the rewrite this step produces.)

Go section by section with before/after as above. When the whole page is done,
tell the user **Step 1 complete**, then **pause ~15 seconds** before starting
Step 2 (e.g. `sleep 15` via Bash, or wait for the user).

### Step 2  -  Push further

Treat Step 1's output as a draft that is still not native enough. Do **not**
look back at the English source. Work only from the current target-language
text. Restructure sentences, swap idioms for stronger native equivalents,
replace weak verbs with strong native ones, drop English-shaped clauses and
noun chains, prefer verbal constructions where the language favors verbs, vary
sentence length the way a native writes, tighten connectors and rhythm.

Show changes section by section. When done, say **Step 2 complete** and
**pause ~15 seconds** before Step 3.

### Step 3  -  Push further again

Same premise: still not perfect native. Go deeper one more time. Hunt the last
residue of translation: stiff transitions, unidiomatic collocations, anything
that betrays an English skeleton, any flat or generic phrasing a top editor
would cut. Sharpen word choice and cadence to native-editor finish.

Show changes section by section. When done, say **Step 3 complete** and give a
one-line summary of the page's final state.

## Closing checks

After Step 3, before declaring done:

- Re-scan for unaccented copy, half-width punctuation inside native sentences,
  English slugs under a non-English locale, and any host-project banned words
  or characters.
- Confirm every SEO field was actually rewritten and now reads native: title,
  meta description, og:title/og:description/og:image:alt,
  twitter:title/twitter:description, schema name/headline/description, and all
  alt text. None should still read like the English source.
- Confirm structure, frontmatter keys, IDs, and component props are untouched
  (unless the user approved a change). Slugs stay as-is unless the user
  approved a rename plus redirect.
- Do **not** run a build unless the user asks.
- Do **not** propagate the rewrite to other locales unless the user says so.

# HubStudio Website Image Style Guide

## Guiding principle

Every image on the site should feel like it was made by a real photographer with a real point of view, then finished in a real studio. Not "AI imagery." Authored work. The website is the proof of what we sell, so the visuals must clear the bar we hold our client deliverables to.

## Every asset carries a creative angle

Creative is the product. So nothing visual on the site is allowed to be merely functional or generic. This rule covers **every** asset, not just photography: SVG icons, illustrations, logos and marks, diagrams, backgrounds, textures, dividers, loaders, empty states, favicons, animation. If it renders on a page, it must have a deliberate creative point of view.

What "a creative angle" means in practice:

- **An idea, not a default.** Each asset expresses a specific concept, mood, or visual wit chosen for that context, never a stock or library default dropped in to fill space.
- **Authored, not assembled.** Even an icon set should read as designed by one hand for hubStudio, with consistent line weight, corner treatment, grid, and personality, not Material/Feather icons used raw.
- **SVG is design work, not plumbing.** Custom SVGs get the same intentionality as a hero photo: considered composition, motion where it earns attention, a reason to exist. Reject the generic.
- **It must defend the headline.** If a teammate asked "why this asset, why here," there is a one-sentence creative answer.

A purely decorative or off-the-shelf asset with no point of view does not ship. When the obvious choice is generic, redesign it or cut it.

## The overall aesthetic

Think *editorial campaign photography, 2024–2026 era*: the visual language of brands like Aesop, Jacquemus, Loewe, Bottega, Hermès, Camper, Arc'teryx. Confident, restrained, warm. Real light, real texture, real distance between camera and subject.

Avoid at all costs: the over-lit, over-saturated, hyper-symmetrical "AI generator default." No glossy plastic skin, no perfect bokeh halos, no impossible reflections, no busy maximalist compositions, no generic stock-photo smiling teams around a laptop.

## Photographic references to anchor each section

**Hero and brand-level imagery**: in the spirit of *Annie Leibovitz* for narrative authority, *Viviane Sassen* for color and shadow, and *Harley Weir* for editorial humanity. Single subjects, generous negative space, decisive light from one direction. The kind of image that earns the headline next to it.

**Case studies and client work**: *Steven Meisel* and *Mario Sorrenti* territory for fashion, *Carl Kleiner* and *Bobby Doherty* for product, *Maurizio Cattelan / Pierpaolo Ferrari (Toiletpaper)* when we want playful campaign energy. The fashion lookbook references we already have in deck (the puffer-vest sequence) sit perfectly in this lane.

**Process and "how we work" sections**: *Wolfgang Tillmans* and *Annie Collinge* for the documentary, in-studio feel. Hands on keyboards, GPU rigs glowing in a dim room, monitors with frames in progress. Shot like reportage, not corporate.

**Talent and team pages**: *Platon* for tight, character-rich portraits when we want gravitas, *Tyler Mitchell* when we want warmth and cultural specificity. Never the cliché "smiling consultant in a white shirt" stock look.

**eCommerce and lifestyle examples**: *Petra Collins* for soft daylight intimacy, *Charlie Engman* for slightly off-center modern still life, *Daniel Arnold* for street-level lifestyle realism.

**Abstract and concept imagery** (for AI capability sections): *Andreas Gursky* for scale, *Hiroshi Sugimoto* for stillness, *Wes Anderson*-coded symmetry only when the section calls for charm rather than seriousness.

## Technical look and feel

Shot on full-frame, prime lens vocabulary: 35mm for environmental, 50mm for portraits, 85mm for product hero, 24mm sparingly for architecture. Shallow but not extreme depth of field: f/2.8 to f/5.6 reads more credible than f/1.2 dreaminess.

Light is the single most important signal of "real." Use directional natural light (window light, golden hour, overcast diffusion) or a single strobe with a softbox. One light source casts one shadow. Avoid the AI tell of multiple competing light sources and glow-from-nowhere.

Color grading: warm shadows, slightly desaturated mid-tones, gentle film emulation (Portra 400, Kodak Gold, Fuji 400H as reference). Black point lifted slightly: pure black reads digital. Skin tones retain texture; pores, freckles, small asymmetries left intact.

Grain: subtle film grain across all hero images. This is the single most effective tactic for defeating AI-detection because it overlays a natural noise pattern the generators don't reproduce convincingly on their own.

## Composition rules

Compose for the rule of thirds, not dead center. Let subjects breathe: generous negative space on at least one side, designed to hold website typography. Crop tighter than feels comfortable; AI defaults toward "fits everything in the frame," real photographers cut into the subject.

Mix scales across the page. A wide environmental shot, then an intimate hand detail, then a portrait. Monotony of crop is what makes pages feel AI-generated even when individual images look fine.

## Subject matter direction by service vertical

For **Fashion and Beauty**: editorial lookbook energy. Single model, considered styling, architectural or natural backdrop. Reference the puffer-vest sequence already in our materials: clean, repeatable, on-figure, no fussy retouching.

For **eCommerce and Retail**: context over isolation. Product in a kitchen, on a desk, in a hand, in afternoon light. The Aesop bottle shot in dried wildflowers (already in our deck) is exactly the register.

For **Automotive and Industrial**: landscape-scale, cinematic. Single vehicle, vast environment, top-down or wide profile, dust and light doing the storytelling. The desert Porsche shot in our existing materials sets the bar.

For **Food and CPG**: *Carl Kleiner* clean geometry or *Bobby Doherty* playful pop, picked deliberately per brand. Hard light, real shadows, ingredients with imperfect surfaces.

For **Tech and B2B**: humans first, screens second. People making things in real workspaces. Avoid the floating-hologram-interface trope entirely.

## A short list of AI tells to strip out

Symmetrical faces with poreless skin. Hands with subtle anatomical drift. Identical reflections in both eyes. Background text that's almost-but-not-quite words. Perfectly aligned books on a shelf. Jewelry that melts into skin. Hair that has no flyaways. Identical bokeh circles. Watermark-like artifacts at edges. Plants with leaves that don't connect to stems.

Every image gets a final human pass to catch these before it goes live.

## Workflow for generating site images

Use a photographer reference and a specific real-world lighting condition to frame the brief in your head, then translate that into concrete descriptive language for the prompt you actually send. A prompt built from "single window light from camera left, warm slightly desaturated grade, mid-afternoon, shallow depth of field, fine grain" outperforms a vague "cinematic and moody."

**Never put a real person's name in a generation prompt (permanent).** The image model behind `scripts/generate-image.mjs` (gpt-image-2, called directly on the OpenAI API) rejects prompts that name photographers, artists, directors, celebrities, or any real individual: it flags them as "potentially sensitive" and the job fails. The photographer names throughout this guide are internal art-direction shorthand only. When you write the literal prompt, convert every named reference into its concrete visual properties: lens, light direction and quality, color grade, grain, composition, distance, mood. Describe the look, never the name.

Generate, then take the best frame into postproduction the way a real photographer would: subtle dodge and burn, film grain pass, slight chromatic aberration at edges, color grade in Lightroom or Capture One presets. This postproduction stage is what closes the gap between "AI image" and "campaign image" and what makes detection tools unreliable against the final file.

Save final assets with realistic EXIF and natural filenames (camera model, date, frame number) rather than the generator's default string.

    "a": "Start from one master with no words in it and room for the longest language. Add each market's headline and legal line as an editable text layer, saved as a separate copy per market. Change the person or the setting only where a market needs it, with an edit that keeps the product. Then send each version to a reviewer in that market."

    "q": "Should I put text in the image or add it on top?",

/**
 * Dictionaries of the French and Chinese pages (see src/i18n/index.ts).
 *
 *   npm run i18n -- extract   read every English page from the running dev
 *                             server and bring the dictionaries in step: new
 *                             sentences are added empty, sentences gone from
 *                             the page are dropped, translations are kept
 *                             (and reused when the same sentence exists
 *                             elsewhere). A sentence on COMMON_MIN_PAGES pages
 *                             or more goes to common.json.
 *   npm run i18n -- check     same reading, writes nothing; fails on an empty
 *                             or missing translation and on a translation that
 *                             breaks the house rules (placeholders, dashes,
 *                             French spacing, Chinese punctuation).
 *   --context <dir>           extract also writes, per page, the English units
 *                             in reading order with their tag (for translators).
 *   --only <path,...>         limit to some English pages.
 *
 * Password-gated pages: set I18N_COOKIE to their gate cookies, or only
 * their sign-in screen is read. With it, each page is read signed out and
 * signed in, and the dictionary keeps the sentences of both views: always
 * extract with I18N_COOKIE set, or the signed-in sentences are dropped.
 *
 * Dev server: I18N_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:4341; bearingbridge.com uses

async function fetchPage(path, gated = false) {
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= 3; attempt++) {
    try {
      // I18N_COOKIE opens the password-gated pages (their gate cookies).
      const headers = { 'accept-language': 'en', ...(gated ? { cookie: process.env.I18N_COOKIE } : {}) };
      const res = await fetch(BASE + path, { headers });
      if (res.ok) return await res.text();
      throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
    } catch (err) {
      if (attempt === 3) throw new Error(`${path}: ${err.message} (is the dev server up at ${BASE}?)`);
    }
  }
}

const pages = new Map(); // en path -> [{key, tag, attr}]
const queue = [...paths];
await Promise.all(
  Array.from({ length: 4 }, async () => {
    while (queue.length) {
      const path = queue.shift();
      // A gated page is read signed out (its sign-in screen) and, with
      // I18N_COOKIE, signed in; its dictionary keeps both views.
      const views = [await fetchPage(path)];
      if (process.env.I18N_COOKIE) {
        const inside = await fetchPage(path, true);
        if (inside !== views[0]) views.push(inside);
      }
      const seen = new Set();
      const units = views
        .flatMap((html) => extractKeys(html, { dataAttrs: DATA_ATTRS }))
        .filter((u) => !seen.has(u.key) && seen.add(u.key));
      pages.set(path, units);
    }
  }),
);

## Two rules that override everything else

1. **Publish market figures, never hubStudio rate figures.** Cost content
   cites third-party benchmarks and category-level ranges. hubStudio's own
   numbers stay in the calculator output and the first call. Search the
   finished file for `$` and check every hit.
2. **China platform specs come from primary evidence only.** Seller backend
   screenshots, live app captures, real rejection notices. If it cannot be
   verified, it does not go on the page. Publish the range and the conflict
   instead.

## The one conflict you must resolve

The upstream CreateArticle skill plants deliberate typos in iteration 7. The
house copy at `.claude/skills/createarticle/` replaces that with a cadence
pass, and the rule stands on its own: **no deliberate errors, ever.** No
planted misspellings, no missing apostrophes, no then/than swaps. Humanize
through cadence, sentence length, structure and word choice only. Say in the
log that iteration 7 ran as the cadence variant.

If a draft contains planted errors, the skill was ignored. Rerun iteration 7.

## Three smaller conflicts, already decided

1. **SEO ceilings.** `content-quality-us` says title under 60 and meta under
   156. The house ceilings are tighter: title 52, meta 152, excerpt 25 words.
   The tighter number wins. Count, do not estimate.
2. **Body text size.** The repo's permanent rule is that running body copy uses
   `var(--type-body)`, never `var(--type-small)`. That binds the publish step
   when it writes the `.astro` page.
3. **No numbers in cards.** The repo's permanent rule bans a decorative ordinal
   inside any repeated titled block. That binds any card grid, step list or
   accordion the publish step generates from an article.

# hubStudio positioning and messaging (binding)

The single source for what hubstudio.ai says and how the site is organized.
Updated October 21, 2026, for the two-pillar architecture (Creative assets and
Social networks) across both the App (the core) and Services (our added value).
Every page, component, meta tag, alt text and llms file follows it. When a page
disagrees with this file, the page is wrong.

## The one idea

hubStudio is built around **two complementary pillars** across both the **app**
(the core) and **our services** (our added value):

- **Pillar · Creative assets**: text, images, and videos.
- **Pillar · Social networks**: posts, campaigns, publishing, paid social, and
  executive advocacy across Western and Chinese networks.

**Use the app on your own, or work with our team inside the app.** The app is
the core. Our services are the added value on top of it: our creatives and
social managers work with you inside the same workspace, where you validate and
publish.

Order of importance on the site: **the app comes first** (the primary action
everywhere is creating an account), **our services come a close second** (the
secondary action everywhere is sending a brief). Neither is an afterthought, and
every page expresses how the app and our services complete each other.

## The two offers & two pillars

### The hubStudio app (the core)

A web app where a person or a team creates creative assets (text, images, video)
with the AI engines of several makers, edits them, organizes campaigns, drafts
and schedules social network posts across Western and Chinese channels, and runs
client or team approvals in Validation. Self-serve, open sign-up.

- Address: `https://hubstudio.bearingbridge.com` (sign-up `/signup`, sign-in
  `/login`). Use the constants in `src/lib/links.ts`, never a hard-coded URL.
- Help center: `/help` on this site (synced from the app repo, do not edit it
  by hand).

### Our services (the added value)

The human creative and social team working inside hubStudio across the same two
pillars:

- **Services · Creative assets**: senior art directors, designers, retouchers,
  motion designers, writers and AIGC specialists working across twenty studio
  service lines (`/services/design/*`). Brand-trained models and GPU pipelines
  run by the studio team.
- **Services · Social networks**: social strategists, editors, community
  managers and media buyers who run your presence across Western networks
  (LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X, YouTube) and Chinese networks
  (WeChat, RedNote, Douyin, Weibo). Three service areas:
  - **Content & page management**: editorial positioning, monthly content
    calendars, post writing, visuals/carousels/short video, community
    management, and scheduling in the app.
  - **Paid social & advertising**: campaign strategy, ad formats, audience
    targeting, retargeting, A/B testing, and media optimization.
  - **Consulting, advocacy & training**: executive ghostwriting, employee
    advocacy programs, channel audits, and hands-on workshops.

Hong Kong headquarters; studios in Shanghai and Changsha and a team in the
Philippines; an office in Paris.

## The two ways to work (locked names)

Use these names verbatim wherever the choice is presented. Never number them.

| Name | Who does the work | What the customer does | Primary action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Use the app** | The customer's own team (client alone) | Creates assets, plans campaigns, and publishes to social networks in hubStudio, paying as it goes from a prepaid balance | Create your account |
| **Work with us in the app** | Client + our team working together in hubStudio | Our team creates assets, writes posts, and runs social campaigns inside the app; the customer reviews, validates, and publishes in Client space or its own workspace | Send a brief |

How **Work with us in the app** works, and only this (it is what the app really
supports):

- **In our workspace (Client space).** Our team works in its own hubStudio
  workspace, tags the assets and social posts "Made for" the customer, and gives
  the customer's people client logins. They see a **Client space** with only the
  finished work and scheduled posts made for them: they download assets,
  comment, and approve or send items back in **Validation**. They never see
  prompts, engines or costs, and they hold no balance.
- **In the customer's workspace.** The customer has its own hubStudio team and
  adds our creatives and social managers as members. We create assets and
  schedule posts from their workspace and their balance; their admins approve in
  Validation; everything stays in their History, Assets Library and publishing
  queue when the project ends.
- Versions (v1, v2 and so on) stay on one approval thread, and nothing on that
  thread can be deleted, so the record of who approved what is permanent.

There is **no "order from the studio" button inside the app**. Never claim one.
A service engagement starts with a brief sent through `/contact`.

/**
 * HowtoLayout: shared shell for every /resources/how-to/<slug> guide.
 * The page passes only `slug`; all meta comes from src/data/howtos.ts.
 * Body markup goes in the default slot and is styled by `.prose` below.
 *
 * Allowed body elements (styled here, nothing else needed):
 *   <p>                                body paragraph
 *   <p class="standfirst">             larger opening paragraph
 *   <h2> / <h3>                        section / sub headings
 *   <ul><li>                           bullet list (use for sequences too)
 *   <li><strong>Label.</strong> copy   titled list row
 *   <blockquote>                       pull quote
 *   <blockquote class="evidence">      cited evidence, set at reading size
 *   <p class="source">                 attribution line under an evidence quote
 *   <div class="callout">              emphasised aside box
 *   <div class="table-wrap"><table>    comparison table, scrolls when narrow
 *   <div class="prompt">               prompt example, with .prompt__label + .prompt__body
 *   <figure><img><figcaption>          screenshot or picture, full prose width,
 *                                      height auto, optional caption beneath
 *
 * Figures: the img fills the prose column at its own aspect ratio (give it
 * width and height attributes so the space is reserved before it loads), with
 * the rounded frame app captures use elsewhere on the site. The figcaption is a
 * caption, so it takes --type-small; running copy never does.
 *
 * Props beyond `slug` are optional and leave the hand-built guides unchanged:
 *   ctaLabel  label of the closing button. "Create your account" (any label
 *             naming an account) switches the closing card to the app door and
 *             links the sign-up page; any other label keeps the studio card.
 *   faq       question and answer pairs for FAQPage schema. They must match
 *             the visible FAQ copy word for word.
 */

}

  <p class="standfirst">The words are the hard part of localizing a visual. A headline baked into the picture has to be rebuilt for every language, and translated copy usually needs more room than the English box it replaces. Plan for both before the first render.</p>

  <h2>How do you localize images for different markets?</h2>

  <p>Make one clean master with no words in it and room left for the longest language. Add each market's text as an editable layer, render text into the picture only when it belongs to the scene, and change casting or setting only where a market needs it. In hubStudio, that's the image studio, the free Image editor and Campaigns.</p>

  <p>The first decision is where the words live.</p>

  <div class="table-wrap">
    <table>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th scope="col">Question</th>
          <th scope="col">Text on top, as an overlay</th>
          <th scope="col">Text rendered in the image</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">What fixing one word costs</th>
          <td>Nothing: edit the layer and save again</td>
          <td>A new run, then a fresh proof</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">How exact the words are</th>
          <td>Exactly what you typed</td>
          <td>What the engine drew; read every character</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Several languages</th>
          <td>One master, one copy per language</td>
          <td>One run or one edit per language</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Brand type, prices, legal lines</th>
          <td>Yes, set from approved copy</td>
          <td>No</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Where it wins</th>
          <td>Headlines, offers, anything a reviewer may change</td>
          <td>A sign, a label or packaging that sits inside the scene</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <p>Past two or three markets, the overlay route is easier to control. The rendered route earns its place when flat type would look pasted on.</p>

  <h2>What goes into a master you can localize?</h2>

  <p>Everything that stays the same in every market, and nothing that doesn't. The product, the light, the framing and the mood are shared. Words are not. Whether people and places travel depends on the market.</p>

  <p>Leave room for the text. Translated copy usually needs more space than the English it came from: plan the headline area for French or German, not for English. Chinese needs the opposite caution. It often takes fewer characters, but each one is taller and more detailed, so it needs height and a size large enough to read. Don't shrink the box because the line got shorter.</p>

  <blockquote class="evidence">The W3C's internationalization guidance says text translated from English or Chinese "will typically be longer in the translation than the original," and that Chinese, Japanese and Korean often need more height than Latin type even when they use fewer characters.</blockquote>
  <p class="source">Source: W3C Internationalization, "Text size in translation," updated February 2016, standards-body guidance. https://www.w3.org/International/articles/article-text-size</p>

  <p>The same page puts the layout rule plainly.</p>

  <blockquote class="evidence">"Be especially careful about fitting text snugly into graphic designs. Separate presentation and content, so that font sizes, line heights, etc. can be easily adapted for translated text."</blockquote>
  <p class="source">Source: W3C Internationalization, "Text size in translation," updated February 2016, standards-body guidance. https://www.w3.org/International/articles/article-text-size</p>

  <p>In the image studio, render the master with the Text to image job, or with Edit an image when you start from your own product photo. Ask for empty space by name.</p>

  <div class="prompt">
    <p class="prompt__label">Prompt example: a textless master</p>
    <p class="prompt__body">A ceramic pour-over coffee set on a pale limestone counter, morning window light from the left, one soft shadow falling right. Keep the product sharp and centered on the lower right third. Leave the upper left half as calm, even, out-of-focus wall for a headline added later, with room for two lines. No text, no letters, no signage, no logos anywhere in the frame.</p>
  </div>

  <p>The price shows before every run, and a failed run isn't charged.</p>

  <h2>What should change in a visual from one market to the next?</h2>

  <p>Start from what stays. Sort every element before anything is rendered, and keep the list with the brief.</p>

  <div class="table-wrap">
    <table>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th scope="col">Element</th>
          <th scope="col">Keep or change</th>
          <th scope="col">How</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Product</th>
          <td>Keep</td>
          <td>Never regenerated per market; it stays from the master</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Light, framing, palette</th>
          <td>Keep</td>
          <td>Shared by every version</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Headline and offer copy</th>
          <td>Change</td>
          <td>Overlay layer per language, from the approved copy deck</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Legal line or required label</th>
          <td>Change where a market requires it</td>
          <td>Overlay from the legal team's approved wording</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Casting</th>
          <td>Change only if the market needs it</td>
          <td>Edit an image with source pictures</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Setting and props</th>
          <td>Change only if the market needs it</td>
          <td>Edit an image, product kept</td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Text inside the scene (a sign, a label)</th>
          <td>Change per language</td>
          <td>Rendered in, then proofed by a native reader</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

  <p>Write the reason next to every "change." When nobody can give one, the element stays as it is in the master.</p>

  <h2>How do you add each market's text as a layer you can edit?</h2>

  <p>Open the master in the Image editor. It's free and runs in your browser; you can open it from the image studio, History or the Assets Library.</p>

  <ul>
    <li>Click Add text, or double-click the picture where the line should go, then type the first market's copy.</li>
    <li>Pick the font and size, then bold, italic or underline and the alignment.</li>
    <li>Set the color. A dark outline or a soft shadow keeps light words readable on a light picture; a highlight behind the words works on a busy one.</li>
    <li>Place the brand logo from the Picture panel, in one of nine positions.</li>
    <li>Open Save, type a name that says the market (for example, "spring master FR 4x5"), and pick Save a copy in the Assets Library. The master stays as it was.</li>
    <li>Go back to the master and repeat for the next language.</li>
  </ul>

  <figure>
    <img src="/Images/help/image-editor-draw.webp" alt="The Image editor with a caption reading New season and a red arrow on the picture, the Draw panel open on the selected arrow" width="1440" height="900" loading="lazy" decoding="async" />
    <figcaption>A caption stays a separate piece, movable and editable, until you save.</figcaption>
  </figure>

  <p>Each caption stays a separate piece until you save, so you can move it, restyle it or rewrite it, with up to 60 steps of undo. Before saving a copy meant for a network, the Social panel checks whether the words are large enough to read on a phone and whether anything sits under the network's buttons.</p>

  <figure>
    <img src="/Images/help/image-editor-save.webp" alt="The Save the picture panel: name, format, quality, size, then Save a copy in the Assets Library, Save as a new version and Download" width="1440" height="900" loading="lazy" decoding="async" />
    <figcaption>Name each copy for its market, then save it next to the master.</figcaption>
  </figure>

  <p>Brand typefaces need one workaround. The editor sets type from its own font list, so when a line must sit in the exact brand font, export it from the design file as a transparent PNG and place it like a logo. The <a href="/resources/how-to/readable-text-in-ai-images">readable text guide</a>, one of the <a href="/resources/how-to">how-to guides</a>, covers that method in more detail. For ads on Facebook and Instagram, the <a href="/solutions/platforms/meta">Meta platform page</a> covers production in the formats Meta serves.</p>

  <h2>When should the text be rendered into the image?</h2>

  <p>When the words belong to the scene. A shop sign, a bottle label or a printed bag looks real when the engine draws it with the light and the surface, and pasted on when it's typed over the top. The help center notes that the ChatGPT Image engines in the app write legible text inside the picture.</p>

  <p>Two app features help. In Skills, the Catalog holds a skill called Legible text inside an image, plus an Avoid list for hands, text artifacts and watermarks. Add them to My skills and Improve with AI follows them each time it rewrites a prompt.</p>

  <p>Some engines can also translate words already in a picture. Their makers say where that goes wrong.</p>

  <blockquote class="evidence">Google says Nano Banana 2 can "translate and localize text within an image." Its model page for Nano Banana Pro adds that the model "may struggle with grammar, spelling, cultural nuances, or idiomatic phrases."</blockquote>
  <p class="source">Source: Google launch post, February 26, 2026, and Google DeepMind model page, read October 2026, the maker's own claim and caveat. https://deepmind.google/models/gemini-image/pro/</p>

  <blockquote class="evidence">OpenAI's image generation guide says its GPT Image models "can still struggle with precise text placement and clarity."</blockquote>
  <p class="source">Source: OpenAI image generation guide, read October 2026, the maker's stated limitations. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation</p>

  <p>So treat a rendered translation as a draft. Run it with the Edit an image job and a prompt that changes the words and nothing else.</p>

  <div class="prompt">
    <p class="prompt__label">Prompt example: a label translated in place</p>
    <p class="prompt__body">Replace the label text "Morning Blend" with "MÃ©lange du matin". Keep the same typeface style, size, color, curve and position on the bag. Change nothing else in the image.</p>
  </div>

  <p>Then a native speaker reads every character at the size the picture will run: accents, apostrophes, line breaks. One wrong letter means another run.</p>

  <h2>How do you change the person or the setting and keep the product?</h2>

  <p>Use Edit an image, not a new render. Upload the master as the first source picture, add reference pictures for the person or the place (up to four sources, depending on the engine), and describe only the change.</p>

  <div class="prompt">
    <p class="prompt__label">Prompt example: a setting changed for one market</p>
    <p class="prompt__body">Keep the coffee set exactly as it is in the first image: same shape, glaze, color, size and position. Replace the limestone counter and wall with a narrow wooden kitchen counter by a tiled wall, as in the second image. Keep the morning light from the left and the empty upper left area. No text.</p>
  </div>

  <p>On the ChatGPT Image engines, an optional mask goes further: its transparent areas mark what may change in the first image, and everything else stays as it is. The Precise image edits skill in the Catalog shapes that kind of instruction. For a person who must look the same across a series, the <a href="/resources/how-to/consistent-character-ai-images-video">consistent character guide</a> shows the method and its limits.</p>

  <p>Check the product after every edit, against the master, at full size.</p>

  <blockquote class="evidence">OpenAI's guide also says its GPT Image models "may occasionally struggle to maintain visual consistency for recurring characters or brand elements across multiple generations."</blockquote>
  <p class="source">Source: OpenAI image generation guide, read October 2026, the maker's stated limitations. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation</p>

  <h2>Which legal lines change from one market to another?</h2>

  <p>Language rules, retouching labels and the wording of a price claim all vary by country, and they touch the layout. France is the clearest case for the text layer.</p>

  <blockquote class="evidence">France's 1994 language law makes French obligatory in written, spoken and audiovisual advertising, and where a translation runs beside it, the French must be "aussi lisible, audible ou intelligible" as the foreign text.</blockquote>
  <p class="source">Source: French Law 94-665 of August 4, 1994, Articles 2 and 4, statute text on Legifrance, read October 10, 2026.</p>

  <p>That's a sizing decision as much as a legal one. Design the French layer at the same weight as the English, not as a small line underneath.</p>

  <p>The <a href="/resources/insights/europe-campaign-localization">article on localizing one campaign for Europe</a> sets out what France, Germany, Spain and Italy each ask of a campaign, from the retouched-photo label to the 30-day prior price on a discount. Headlines that need rewriting rather than translating belong to <a href="/resources/insights/transcreation-as-a-production-line">transcreation, which has its own article</a>. This guide describes production practice, not legal advice.</p>

  <h2>How do you keep every market's version organized and approved?</h2>

  <p>Put the whole launch in one campaign. In the app, a campaign keeps one launch's files under one name and an optional brief. It points at files in the Assets Library and copies nothing, so the master and every market's copy sit side by side. Pick the campaign under Campaign in the image studio before you render, and every picture from that page joins it. The library's Campaign filter then shows the whole set.</p>

  <figure>
    <img src="/Images/help/campaigns-page.webp" alt="A campaign's page: the band with All campaigns, Add assets and Delete the campaign, the name and the brief, the tiles by type, the Name and brief card, and In this campaign with four assets" width="1440" height="1100" loading="lazy" decoding="async" />
    <figcaption>One campaign holds the master and every market's version.</figcaption>
  </figure>

  <p>Send each market's version to that market's reviewer through Validation: a teammate, or one of the client's people when the work is made for a client. They validate it or send it back with a comment, and every version stays on one thread. The app runs in English, French and Chinese, and each person picks their own, so the reviewer in Paris or Shanghai can work in their language. Prompts and files stay in the language they were written in.</p>

  <p><a href="/app/campaigns">Campaigns</a>, Validation and the <a href="/app/image-tools">Image editor</a> cost nothing to use. When a launch runs to dozens of formats and languages, the studio can make the set with you through its <a href="/services/design/ad-creative">ad creative design service</a>.</p>

  <h2>Will your font show accents and Chinese characters?</h2>

  <p>Check before you save, every time. A font that lacks a character shows a small empty box in its place, nicknamed tofu. The project behind Google's Noto fonts took its name from the fix: "no more tofu."</p>

  <ul>
    <li>Type a test line with the accents each market uses: Ã©, Ã¨, Ã§ and Ã  for French; Ã¤, Ã¶, Ã¼ and ÃŸ for German; Ã± and the opening question mark for Spanish.</li>
    <li>For Chinese, type a full headline, not one character, and look for empty boxes anywhere in the line.</li>
    <li>Check the line at the size it will run on a phone.</li>
    <li>If the font fails, set the line in a font that covers the script, or place it as artwork exported from the design file.</li>
  </ul>

  <h2>What should you check before a localized version ships?</h2>

  <p>Run this on every market's file, not just the first one.</p>

  <ul>
    <li>Product identical to the master: shape, color, label, proportions.</li>
    <li>Every word matches the approved copy deck for that market.</li>
    <li>Accents, punctuation and characters render in the chosen font.</li>
    <li>Rendered text read character by character by a native speaker.</li>
    <li>Text clear of the network's buttons and readable on a phone.</li>
    <li>Required legal line or label present, from the approved wording.</li>
    <li>File named for its market and filed in the launch's campaign.</li>
    <li>Sent through Validation to that market's reviewer.</li>
  </ul>

  <h2>Questions about localizing images for different markets</h2>

  <h3>How do I localize an image for different countries?</h3>

  <p>Start from one master with no words in it and room for the longest language. Add each market's headline and legal line as an editable text layer, saved as a separate copy per market. Change the person or the setting only where a market needs it, with an edit that keeps the product. Then send each version to a reviewer in that market.</p>

  <h3>Should I put text in the image or add it on top?</h3>

  <p>Add it on top when the words must be exact or may change: headlines, offers, prices, legal lines, anything translated. Fixing a layer costs nothing. Render it into the image when the text belongs to the scene, such as a sign or a label, and proof every character, because a correction means a new run.</p>

  <h3>Can AI translate the text inside an image?</h3>

  <p>Some engines can. Google says Nano Banana 2 can translate and localize text within an image, and its page for Nano Banana Pro warns the model may struggle with grammar, spelling, cultural nuance and idiom. Use the result as a draft. A native speaker reads it at full size before it goes anywhere.</p>

  <h3>What should change in a visual from one market to another?</h3>

  <p>The words always change: headline, offer and any required legal line. Casting, setting and props change only when there's a reason you can write down for that market. The product, the light and the framing stay the same in every version.</p>

  <h3>How do I keep localized versions organized?</h3>

  <p>Name every copy for its market when you save it, and file the master and all versions in one campaign. In hubStudio a campaign points at Assets Library files without copying them, and the library filters by campaign. Each market's version then goes to its reviewer through Validation, with every version kept on one thread.</p>

  <h3>Do fonts support accents and Chinese characters?</h3>

  <p>Not all of them. A font missing a character shows a small empty box where the letter should be. Type a test line with every accent the market uses, and a full Chinese headline, then check it at the size it will run. If the font fails, use one that covers the script, or place the line as artwork exported from your design file.</p>
</HowtoLayout>

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Pre-commit step: optimize any staged raster images, then re-stage them.
//
// Wired in via .git/hooks/pre-commit. Runs only on files git reports as added
// or modified that fall under the watched directory and have a raster
// extension. Safe to run repeatedly: the batch optimizer keeps the original
// buffer if it can't shrink it.

import { execSync } from "node:child_process";
import path from "node:path";

const RASTER_EXT = new Set([".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".webp"]);
const ROOT_PREFIX = "public/Images/"; // <-- change per project

function staged() {
  // -z + null parser keeps paths with spaces intact.
  const out = execSync("git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR -z", {
    encoding: "buffer",
  });
  return out
    .toString("utf8")
    .split("\0")
    .filter(Boolean);
}

function isTargetImage(p) {
  const norm = p.replace(/\\/g, "/");
  if (!norm.startsWith(ROOT_PREFIX)) return false;
  return RASTER_EXT.has(path.extname(norm).toLowerCase());
}

function main() {
  const files = staged().filter(isTargetImage);
  if (files.length === 0) return;

  console.log(`[pre-commit] optimizing ${files.length} image(s)...`);
  for (const f of files) {
    try {
      execSync(`node scripts/optimize-images-batch.mjs "${f}"`, { stdio: "inherit" });
      execSync(`git add -- "${f}"`, { stdio: "inherit" });
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(`[pre-commit] failed to optimize ${f}: ${err.message}`);
      process.exit(1);
    }
  }
}

main();

+for(const file of files){

+  const old=JSON.parse(original), current=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(release,file),'utf8'));
+  const same=Object.keys(old).length===Object.keys(current).length&&Object.entries(old).every(([k,v])=>current[k]===v);
+  if(same){fs.writeFileSync(path.join(release,file),original);continue;}
+  const ordered={};
+  for(const k of Object.keys(old))if(k in current)ordered[k]=current[k];
+  for(const k of Object.keys(current))if(!(k in ordered))ordered[k]=current[k];
+  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(release,file),JSON.stringify(ordered,null,2)+'\n');
+  retained++;
+}

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),cp=require('child_process');
+const root=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');
+const git=(args,cwd=root,extra={})=>cp.execFileSync('git',['-c','core.safecrlf=false',...args],{cwd,encoding:'utf8',stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe'],maxBuffer:64*1024*1024,...extra});
+if(git(['diff','--cached','--name-only']).trim())throw Error('Main index is not empty');
+if(git(['rev-parse','HEAD']).trim()!==git(['rev-parse','HEAD'],release).trim())throw Error('Release and main bases differ');
+const files=git(['ls-files','--modified','--others','--exclude-standard'],release).trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean);
+const baseFiles=new Set(git(['ls-tree','-r','--name-only','HEAD']).trim().split('\n'));
+for(const file of files){
+  const from=path.join(release,file),to=path.join(root,file);
+  if(file.startsWith('editorial/logs/runs/'))continue;
+  if(file.startsWith('src/i18n/dict/')&&baseFiles.has(file)){
+    const base=JSON.parse(git(['show','HEAD:'+file]));
+    const next=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(from,'utf8'));
+    const current=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(to,'utf8'));
+    let changed=false;
+    for(const [key,value] of Object.entries(next)){
+      if(base[key]===value)continue;
+      if(current[key]&&current[key]!==base[key]&&current[key]!==value)throw Error('Concurrent translation conflict in '+file+': '+key);
+      if(current[key]!==value){current[key]=value;changed=true;}
+    }
+    for(const key of Object.keys(base)){
+      if(!(key in next)&&current[key]===base[key]){delete current[key];changed=true;}
+    }
+    if(changed)fs.writeFileSync(to,JSON.stringify(current,null,2)+'\n');
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(file==='src/i18n/routes.ts'||file.startsWith('src/i18n/glossary/')){
+    const patch=git(['diff','--binary','--full-index','--',file],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    git(['apply','--check','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    git(['apply','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(baseFiles.has(file)&&!file.startsWith('editorial/')){
+    const baseline=git(['show','HEAD:'+file],root,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    const current=fs.readFileSync(to);
+    if(current.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')!==baseline.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')&&!current.equals(fs.readFileSync(from)))throw Error('Unexpected existing source change: '+file);
+  }
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(to),{recursive:true});fs.copyFileSync(from,to);
+}
+git(['add','--',...files],release);
+git(['diff','--cached','--check'],release);
+const patch=git(['diff','--cached','--binary','--full-index'],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+git(['apply','--cached','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+const mainTree=git(['write-tree']).trim(),releaseTree=git(['write-tree'],release).trim();
+if(mainTree!==releaseTree)throw Error('Release and main staged trees differ');
+fs.writeFileSync(path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-staged.json'),JSON.stringify({tree:mainTree,files},null,2));
+console.log('Main staged tree matches validated release: '+mainTree);

/**
 * RSS 2.0 feed of every resource hubStudio publishes: the insights and the
 * how-to guides, merged newest first. One feed per locale:
 *
 *   https://www.hubstudio.ai/resources/rss.xml           English
 *   https://www.hubstudio.ai/fr/ressources/rss.xml       French
 *   https://www.hubstudio.ai/zh/resources/rss.xml        Chinese
 *
 * Built from src/data/insights.ts and src/data/howtos.ts, so a resource
 * enters the feeds the moment it is added there. The French and Chinese
 * titles, decks and categories come from the same dictionaries that
 * translate the pages (src/i18n/dict), and the links from the French
 * addresses in src/i18n/routes.ts: a feed item reads exactly like the page
 * it points to. Built by hand (no @astrojs/rss) to honour the self-host rule.
 *
 * The older insights-only feed (/resources/insights/rss.xml) stays as it is:
 * the LinkedIn auto-poster reads it.
 */
import { insights } from '../data/insights';
import { howtos } from '../data/howtos';
import { dictionaryFor, pathIn, HTML_LANG, type Locale } from '../i18n/index';

const SITE = 'https://www.hubstudio.ai';

export const RESOURCES_FEED: Record<Locale, string> = {
  en: '/resources/rss.xml',
  fr: '/fr/ressources/rss.xml',
  zh: '/zh/resources/rss.xml',
};

  en: 'hubStudio Resources',
  fr: 'Ressources hubStudio',
  zh: 'hubStudio èµ„æº',

/** Escape the five XML predefined entities for use in element text. */
function esc(value: string): string {
  return value
    .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;')
    .replace(/"/g, '&quot;')
    .replace(/'/g, '&apos;');
}

/** Text as Astro renders it into the page: the form the dictionary keys take. */
function htmlEscape(value: string): string {
  return value
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim()
    .replace(/&/g, '&amp;')
    .replace(/</g, '&lt;')
    .replace(/>/g, '&gt;')
    .replace(/"/g, '&quot;')
    .replace(/'/g, '&#39;');
}

/** A dictionary value back to plain text: placeholders dropped, entities read. */
function plain(value: string): string {
  return value
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')
    .replace(/&#(\d+);/g, (_, n) => String.fromCodePoint(Number(n)))
    .replace(/&#x([0-9a-f]+);/gi, (_, n) => String.fromCodePoint(parseInt(n, 16)))
    .replace(/&nbsp;/g, 'Â ')
    .replace(/&quot;/g, '"')
    .replace(/&lt;/g, '<')
    .replace(/&gt;/g, '>')
    .replace(/&amp;/g, '&');
}

/** ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to an RFC-822 date string, as RSS pubDate wants. */
function rfc822(dateISO: string): string {
  return new Date(`${dateISO}T00:00:00Z`).toUTCString();
}

/** MIME type for an enclosure, inferred from the file extension. */
function imageType(path: string): string {
  const ext = path.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase();
  if (ext === 'png') return 'image/png';
  if (ext === 'jpg' || ext === 'jpeg') return 'image/jpeg';
  if (ext === 'avif') return 'image/avif';
  return 'image/webp';
}

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),cp=require('child_process');
+const root=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');
+const git=(args,cwd=root,extra={})=>cp.execFileSync('git',['-c','core.safecrlf=false',...args],{cwd,encoding:'utf8',stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe'],maxBuffer:64*1024*1024,...extra});
+if(git(['diff','--cached','--name-only']).trim())throw Error('Main index is not empty');
+if(git(['rev-parse','HEAD']).trim()!==git(['rev-parse','HEAD'],release).trim())throw Error('Release and main bases differ');
+const files=git(['ls-files','--modified','--others','--exclude-standard'],release).trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean);
+const baseFiles=new Set(git(['ls-tree','-r','--name-only','HEAD']).trim().split('\n'));
+for(const file of files){
+  const from=path.join(release,file),to=path.join(root,file);
+  if(file.startsWith('editorial/logs/runs/'))continue;
+  if(file.startsWith('src/i18n/dict/')&&baseFiles.has(file)){
+    const base=JSON.parse(git(['show','HEAD:'+file]));
+    const next=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(from,'utf8'));
+    const current=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(to,'utf8'));
+    let changed=false;
+    for(const [key,value] of Object.entries(next)){
+      if(base[key]===value)continue;
+      if(current[key]&&current[key]!==base[key]&&current[key]!==value)throw Error('Concurrent translation conflict in '+file+': '+key);
+      if(current[key]!==value){current[key]=value;changed=true;}
+    }
+    for(const key of Object.keys(base)){
+      if(!(key in next)&&current[key]===base[key]){delete current[key];changed=true;}
+    }
+    if(changed)fs.writeFileSync(to,JSON.stringify(current,null,2)+'\n');
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(file==='src/i18n/routes.ts'||file.startsWith('src/i18n/glossary/')){
+    const patch=git(['diff','--binary','--full-index','--',file],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    git(['apply','--check','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    git(['apply','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(baseFiles.has(file)&&!file.startsWith('editorial/')){
+    const baseline=git(['show','HEAD:'+file],root,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    const current=fs.readFileSync(to);
+    if(current.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')!==baseline.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')&&!current.equals(fs.readFileSync(from)))throw Error('Unexpected existing source change: '+file);
+  }
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(to),{recursive:true});fs.copyFileSync(from,to);
+}
+git(['add','--',...files],release);
+git(['diff','--cached','--check'],release);
+const patch=git(['diff','--cached','--binary','--full-index'],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+git(['apply','--cached','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});

+  const indexRoute=locale==='fr'?'fr/ressources/guides-pratiques':locale==='zh'?'zh/resources/how-to':'resources/how-to';

+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');

+    const current=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(to,'utf8'));
+    let changed=false;

+    git(['apply','--check','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});

+    continue;
+  }
+  if(baseFiles.has(file)&&!file.startsWith('editorial/')){

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),cp=require('child_process');
+const root=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');
+const baseline=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-baseline');

+const staged=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-staged.json'),'utf8'));
+const touched=new Set(staged.files);
+let exact=0,dicts=0;

+  const before=fs.readFileSync(path.join(baseline,f));
+  const now=fs.readFileSync(path.join(root,f));

+    if(!before.equals(now))throw Error('Unrelated file changed: '+f);
+    exact++;continue;
+  }

+    }
+    dicts++;

+  }
+}

+  const article=schemas.find(s=>s['@type']==='Article');

+  check(faq?.mainEntity?.length===6,'Wrong FAQ count '+locale);
+  check(html.querySelectorAll('main table').length===2,'Wrong table count '+locale);
+  if(locale!=='en')check(!source.includes('The words are the hard part of localizing a visual.'),'Untranslated opening '+locale);
+  const indexRoute=locale==='fr'?'fr/ressources/guides-pratiques':locale==='zh'?'zh/resources/how-to':'resources/how-to';
+  const index=parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(base,indexRoute,'index.html'),'utf8'));
+  check(index.querySelector('a.feat')?.getAttribute('href')===route,'Guide not featured '+locale);
+  console.log(`${locale}: ${h1}; canonical, language alternates, hero, three localized captures, two tables, six FAQ entries, date and featured listing verified`);

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),cp=require('child_process');
+const root=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');
+const git=(args,cwd=root,extra={})=>cp.execFileSync('git',['-c','core.safecrlf=false',...args],{cwd,encoding:'utf8',stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe'],maxBuffer:64*1024*1024,...extra});
+if(git(['diff','--cached','--name-only']).trim())throw Error('Main index is not empty');
+if(git(['rev-parse','HEAD']).trim()!==git(['rev-parse','HEAD'],release).trim())throw Error('Release and main bases differ');
+const files=git(['ls-files','--modified','--others','--exclude-standard'],release).trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean);
+const baseFiles=new Set(git(['ls-tree','-r','--name-only','HEAD']).trim().split('\n'));
+for(const file of files){
+  const from=path.join(release,file),to=path.join(root,file);
+  if(file.startsWith('editorial/logs/runs/'))continue;
+  if(file.startsWith('src/i18n/dict/')&&baseFiles.has(file)){
+    const base=JSON.parse(git(['show','HEAD:'+file]));
+    const next=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(from,'utf8'));
+    const current=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(to,'utf8'));
+    let changed=false;
+    for(const [key,value] of Object.entries(next)){
+      if(base[key]===value)continue;
+      if(current[key]&&current[key]!==base[key]&&current[key]!==value)throw Error('Concurrent translation conflict in '+file+': '+key);
+      if(current[key]!==value){current[key]=value;changed=true;}
+    }
+    for(const key of Object.keys(base)){
+      if(!(key in next)&&current[key]===base[key]){delete current[key];changed=true;}
+    }
+    if(changed)fs.writeFileSync(to,JSON.stringify(current,null,2)+'\n');
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(file==='src/i18n/routes.ts'||file.startsWith('src/i18n/glossary/')){
+    const patch=git(['diff','--binary','--full-index','--',file],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    git(['apply','--check','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    git(['apply','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(baseFiles.has(file)&&!file.startsWith('editorial/')){
+    const baseline=git(['show','HEAD:'+file],root,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    const current=fs.readFileSync(to);
+    if(current.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')!==baseline.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')&&!current.equals(fs.readFileSync(from)))throw Error('Unexpected existing source change: '+file);
+  }
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(to),{recursive:true});fs.copyFileSync(from,to);
+}
+git(['add','--',...files],release);
+git(['diff','--cached','--check'],release);
+const patch=git(['diff','--cached','--binary','--full-index'],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+git(['apply','--cached','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),cp=require('child_process');
+const root=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');
+const baseline=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-baseline');
+const files=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(baseline,'files.json'),'utf8'));
+const staged=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-staged.json'),'utf8'));
+const touched=new Set(staged.files);
+let exact=0,dicts=0;
+for(const f of files){
+  const before=fs.readFileSync(path.join(baseline,f));
+  const now=fs.readFileSync(path.join(root,f));
+  if(!touched.has(f)){
+    if(!before.equals(now))throw Error('Unrelated file changed: '+f);
+    exact++;continue;
+  }
+  if(f.startsWith('src/i18n/dict/')){
+    const base=JSON.parse(cp.execFileSync('git',['show','HEAD:'+f],{cwd:release,encoding:'utf8'}));
+    const prior=JSON.parse(before),current=JSON.parse(now);
+    for(const [key,value] of Object.entries(prior)){
+      if(value!==base[key]&&current[key]!==value)throw Error('Existing translation altered: '+f+': '+key);
+    }

+    if(restored!==before.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n'))throw Error('Unrelated route changes were altered');
+  }
+}

# BRIEF 82: How to localize one visual for several markets

Run with the CreateArticle skill. Read `../CLAUDE.md` (its "Wave two" section
first) and `../SPEC.md`. They override any conflicting rule inside the skill.

**Standing rule.** No competitor is ever named, described, compared to, or alluded to. Market figures are attributed to the category and the date, never to a company. Comparison content compares models of buying and regions, never firms.

## CreateArticle inputs

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| website | https://www.hubstudio.ai |
| audience | people out of China |
| reader stage | practitioner |
| family | How-to (`template: howto` in the draft's frontmatter) |
| brief | this file |

## Target

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Working H1 | How to localize one visual for several markets |
| Slug | `/resources/how-to/localize-visual-for-markets/` |
| Publishes as | how-to guide: `src/pages/resources/how-to/localize-visual-for-markets.astro` on HowtoLayout plus an entry in `src/data/howtos.ts` |
| Output file | `output/localize-visual-for-markets.md` |
| Research file | `research/localize-visual-for-markets.md` |
| Hero image | `public/Images/howto-localize-visual-for-markets.webp`, referenced as `/Images/howto-localize-visual-for-markets.webp` |
| Primary query | `localize images for different markets` |
| Secondary queries | `image localization`, `translate text in image`, `adapt ad creative for different countries`, `localize product images for international markets` |
| SERP verdict | CONCEPTUAL. Localization vendors and image-translation tools rank with 'why it matters' essays (colors, symbols, right-to-left layouts) and a pitch; none gives a production method: what to keep in a master, what to render per market, and how to keep text editable. |
| Body length | 1,700 words (body only, per the char-count rule) |
| Slot requirement | A step sequence, a prompt example, a checklist the reader can use today |

## The angle

Build the visual to be localized before you make it: a clean master with no words in it, text added per market as an editable layer, and casting or setting changed only where the market needs it. This guide is the production method, shown in the hubStudio app, with the cases where rendering the text into the image is the better call.

## The research gate, before any drafting

No body copy until `research/localize-visual-for-markets.md` exists and every claim in it is
marked. Follow R1 to R7 in `../CLAUDE.md`. In short:

- Map what has to be true before looking anything up.

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),cp=require('child_process');
+const root=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');
+const git=(args,cwd=root,extra={})=>cp.execFileSync('git',['-c','core.safecrlf=false',...args],{cwd,encoding:'utf8',stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe'],maxBuffer:64*1024*1024,...extra});
+if(git(['diff','--cached','--name-only']).trim())throw Error('Main index is not empty');
+if(git(['rev-parse','HEAD']).trim()!==git(['rev-parse','HEAD'],release).trim())throw Error('Release and main bases differ');
+const files=git(['ls-files','--modified','--others','--exclude-standard'],release).trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean);
+const baseFiles=new Set(git(['ls-tree','-r','--name-only','HEAD']).trim().split('\n'));
+for(const file of files){
+  const from=path.join(release,file),to=path.join(root,file);
+  if(file.startsWith('editorial/logs/runs/'))continue;
+  if(file.startsWith('src/i18n/dict/')&&baseFiles.has(file)){
+    const base=JSON.parse(git(['show','HEAD:'+file]));
+    const next=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(from,'utf8'));
+    const current=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(to,'utf8'));
+    let changed=false;
+    for(const [key,value] of Object.entries(next)){
+      if(base[key]===value)continue;
+      if(current[key]&&current[key]!==base[key]&&current[key]!==value)throw Error('Concurrent translation conflict in '+file+': '+key);
+      if(current[key]!==value){current[key]=value;changed=true;}
+    }
+    for(const key of Object.keys(base)){
+      if(!(key in next)&&current[key]===base[key]){delete current[key];changed=true;}
+    }
+    if(changed)fs.writeFileSync(to,JSON.stringify(current,null,2)+'\n');
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(file==='src/i18n/routes.ts'||file.startsWith('src/i18n/glossary/')){
+    const patch=git(['diff','--binary','--full-index','--',file],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    git(['apply','--check','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    git(['apply','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+    continue;
+  }
+  if(baseFiles.has(file)&&!file.startsWith('editorial/')){
+    const baseline=git(['show','HEAD:'+file],root,{encoding:'buffer'});
+    const current=fs.readFileSync(to);
+    if(current.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')!==baseline.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n')&&!current.equals(fs.readFileSync(from)))throw Error('Unexpected existing source change: '+file);
+  }
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(to),{recursive:true});fs.copyFileSync(from,to);
+}
+git(['add','--',...files],release);
+git(['diff','--cached','--check'],release);
+const patch=git(['diff','--cached','--binary','--full-index'],release,{encoding:'buffer'});
+git(['apply','--cached','--whitespace=nowarn','-'],root,{input:patch});
+const mainTree=git(['write-tree']).trim(),releaseTree=git(['write-tree'],release).trim();

+const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),cp=require('child_process');
+const root=path.resolve(__dirname,'..');
+const release=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-release');
+const baseline=path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-baseline');
+const files=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(baseline,'files.json'),'utf8'));
+const staged=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname,'publish-2026-10-22-staged.json'),'utf8'));
+const touched=new Set(staged.files);
+let exact=0,dicts=0;
+for(const f of files){
+  const before=fs.readFileSync(path.join(baseline,f));
+  const now=fs.readFileSync(path.join(root,f));
+  if(!touched.has(f)){
+    if(!before.equals(now))throw Error('Unrelated file changed: '+f);
+    exact++;continue;
+  }
+  if(f.startsWith('src/i18n/dict/')){
+    const base=JSON.parse(cp.execFileSync('git',['show','HEAD:'+f],{cwd:release,encoding:'utf8'}));
+    const prior=JSON.parse(before),current=JSON.parse(now);
+    for(const [key,value] of Object.entries(prior)){
+      if(value!==base[key]&&current[key]!==value)throw Error('Existing translation altered: '+f+': '+key);
+    }
+    dicts++;
+  }
+  if(f==='src/i18n/routes.ts'){
+    const restored=now.toString('utf8').replace(/^.*'localize-visual-for-markets'.*\r?\n/m,'').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n');
+    if(restored!==before.toString('utf8').replace(/\r\n/g,'\n'))throw Error('Unrelated route changes were altered');
+  }
+}
+console.log(`${exact} unrelated files preserved byte-for-byte; prior edits in ${dicts} shared dictionaries and the route map preserved.`);

+const slug = 'localize-visual-for-markets';
+const routes = [
